chapter_title: Univariate Data: Box Plots, Quartiles, and Standard Deviation (10 & 10A)

worksheets.title: Box Plots, Outlier Fences, and Comparing Distributions

fluency_questions.prompt: For the ordered dataset of $12$ observations: $5, 19, 21, 23, 25, 26, 28, 30, 31, 33, 35, 52$, find:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The median ($Q_2$), lower quartile ($Q_1$), and upper quartile ($Q_3$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: The interquartile range ($\text{IQR}$) and the lower and upper outlier fences

parts.label: c
parts.question: All formal outliers in the dataset

parts.label: d
parts.question: The endpoints of the left and right whiskers on an outlier box plot (the most extreme non-outlier values)
parts.answer: Left whisker at $19$, right whisker at $35$

fluency_questions.prompt: [10A] A sample of $n = 6$ measurements is $6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16$. Find:

parts.label: c
parts.question: The sample variance $s^2 = \dfrac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}$ and sample standard deviation $s$

parts.label: d
parts.question: The new mean and new sample standard deviation if every measurement is transformed by $y_i = 3x_i - 5$

fluency_questions.prompt: [10A] A sample of $n = 5$ values has sample mean $\bar{x} = 12$ and sample variance $s^2 = 10$. Four of the values are $8, 11, 13, 16$. Find:

parts.label: c
parts.question: The exact sample variance $s^2$ of the $5$ values $8, 11, 12, 13, 16$

parts.label: d
parts.question: The new sample variance if a sixth value equal to the mean ($x_6 = 12$) is appended to $8, 11, 12, 13, 16$

fluency_questions.prompt: [10A] A dataset has mean $\bar{x} = 50$ and standard deviation $s = 8$. Using the z-score formula $z = \dfrac{x - \bar{x}}{s}$, find:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The z-score of a data value $x = 62$

parts.label: b
parts.question: The z-score of a data value $x = 34$

parts.label: c
parts.question: The data value $x$ that lies $2.25$ standard deviations above the mean

parts.label: d
parts.question: The interval $[\bar{x} - 2s, \bar{x} + 2s]$ containing values within $2$ standard deviations of the mean

application_questions.question: A class of $25$ students sits a Chemistry test. The first group of $15$ students has a mean score of $72$, and the remaining $10$ students have a mean score of $82$. Calculate the combined mean score of all $25$ students.

For a dataset of annual rainfall totals (in mm) in Canberra, $Q_1 = 520\text{ mm}$ and the lower outlier fence is $310\text{ mm}$. Work backwards to find the interquartile range ($\text{IQR}$), the upper quartile $Q_3$, and the upper outlier fence.

[10A] An athlete in Perth records a time of $11.2\text{ s}$ in the $100\text{ m}$ sprint (squad mean $11.8\text{ s}$, standard deviation $0.3\text{ s}$) and a jump of $6.40\text{ m}$ in the long jump (squad mean $5.80\text{ m}$, standard deviation $0.25\text{ m}$). Remembering that a lower sprint time is better, compare her relative performance in the two events using z-scores.
application_questions.answer: Sprint $z = \dfrac{11.2 - 11.8}{0.3} = -2.0$ ($2.0$ s.d. faster than the mean); Long jump $z = \dfrac{6.40 - 5.80}{0.25} = +2.4$ ($2.4$ s.d. above the mean). Her long jump performance is relatively stronger.

application_questions.question: [10A] The temperatures of $8$ midday readings in Darwin in $^\circ\text{C}$ have mean $\bar{x} = 32.0^\circ\text{C}$ and sample standard deviation $s = 1.5^\circ\text{C}$. If these temperatures are converted to degrees Fahrenheit using $F = 1.8C + 32$, find the mean and sample standard deviation in $^\circ\text{F}$.

reasoning_questions.question: [10A] Prove algebraically that if every observation in a sample $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ is linearly transformed to $y_i = ax_i + b$ (where $a > 0$ and $b$ are constants), then the sample mean becomes $\bar{y} = a\bar{x} + b$ and the sample standard deviation becomes $s_y = a s_x$ (independent of $b$).
reasoning_questions.answer: $\bar{y} = \frac{1}{n}\sum(ax_i + b) = a\bar{x} + b$. Then $y_i - \bar{y} = (ax_i + b) - (a\bar{x} + b) = a(x_i - \bar{x})$, so $s_y = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum a^2(x_i - \bar{x})^2} = a\sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2} = a s_x$.

reasoning_questions.question: [10A] Prove the computational identity for the sum of squared deviations: $\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2 = \left(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\right) - n\bar{x}^2$, using the fact that $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i = n\bar{x}$.
reasoning_questions.answer: $\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2 = \sum (x_i^2 - 2\bar{x}x_i + \bar{x}^2) = \sum x_i^2 - 2\bar{x}\sum x_i + n\bar{x}^2 = \sum x_i^2 - 2\bar{x}(n\bar{x}) + n\bar{x}^2 = \sum x_i^2 - n\bar{x}^2$.
